question: If a body’s velocity changes from +20 m/s to –10 m/s in 4 seconds, the acceleration is _______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**– 7.5 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Acceleration** is defined as the **rate of change of velocity** of an object with respect to **time**. It is a **vector quantity**, meaning it possesses both **magnitude** and **direction**.
 
• The mathematical formula to calculate **average acceleration (a)** is given by: **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the **final velocity**, **u** is the **initial velocity**, and **t** is the **time interval**.
 
• In the given problem, the **initial velocity (u)** is **+20 m/s**, the **final velocity (v)** is **-10 m/s**, and the **time taken (t)** is **4 seconds**.
 
• Substituting the values into the formula: **a = (-10 m/s - 20 m/s) / 4 s**. This simplifies to **a = -30 / 4**, which equals **-7.5 m/s²**.
 
• The **negative sign** indicates that the **acceleration** is acting in the **opposite direction** to the initial motion, or that the body is experiencing **retardation** relative to the positive direction. ***Hence, the correct answer is – 7.5 m/s².***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **SI Unit of Acceleration**: The standard unit for measuring **acceleration** in the **International System of Units (SI)** is the **meter per second squared (m/s²)**.
 
• **Vector Nature**: Since **velocity** is a vector, any change in either the **speed** or the **direction** of motion results in **acceleration**. In this case, the body not only slowed down but also **reversed its direction** (moving from positive to negative velocity).
 
• **Uniform vs. Non-Uniform Acceleration**: **Uniform acceleration** occurs when the **velocity** changes by equal amounts in equal intervals of **time**. **Non-uniform acceleration** occurs when the rate of change of **velocity** varies over time.
 
• **Retardation/Deceleration**: When the **acceleration** of a body is in the direction opposite to its **velocity**, it is often referred to as **deceleration** or **retardation**. It results in a decrease in the **magnitude** of velocity (speed) until the object stops or reverses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sign Convention**: In physics, **direction** is often indicated by **positive (+)** and **negative (-)** signs. A change from **+20 m/s** to **-10 m/s** implies a total change in **velocity** of **30 m/s** in the negative direction.
 
• **Instantaneous vs. Average**: While the formula **(v-u)/t** provides the **average acceleration** over the **4-second** interval, **instantaneous acceleration** refers to the acceleration at a specific **moment in time**, calculated using **derivatives (dv/dt)**.
 
• **Graphical Representation**: On a **velocity-time graph**, the **slope** of the line represents the **acceleration**. A downward-sloping line indicates **negative acceleration**.
